title: Forms Bootcamp
tagline: Present, Imperfect, Perfect, Pluperfect — Active & Passive
description: Master all four subjunctive tenses in active and passive voice. You'll conjugate every form from scratch and learn to distinguish subjunctive from indicative on sight. This is the foundation for every other module.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person singular present active subjunctive of amare (to love).
questions.hint: Present active subjunctive: change the characteristic vowel. 1st conj. ā → e.
questions.explanation: The present active subjunctive of 1st conjugation verbs replaces the characteristic -ā- with -ē-: amō → amem, ames, amet...

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person plural present active subjunctive of monere (to warn).
questions.hint: Present active subjunctive: 2nd conj. ē → eā. 3pl ending = -nt.
questions.explanation: 2nd conjugation: characteristic -ē- shifts → eā-. 3pl: moneant.

questions.prompt: Give the 2nd person singular present active subjunctive of ducere (to lead).
questions.hint: 3rd conjugation: add -ā- between stem and ending. 2sg = -s.
questions.explanation: 3rd conjugation present subjunctive: dūc- + ā + s = dūcās.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person plural present active subjunctive of audire (to hear).
questions.hint: 4th conjugation: add -ā- after the stem vowel. 1pl = -mus.
questions.explanation: 4th conjugation: aud- + iā + mus = audiāmus.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person singular present active subjunctive of esse (to be).
questions.hint: esse is irregular in the present subjunctive: sim, sis, sit...
questions.explanation: esse: sim, sīs, sit, sīmus, sītis, sint. Memorize these — they appear constantly.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person plural present active subjunctive of esse.
questions.hint: The 3pl of esse's present subjunctive is irregular.
questions.explanation: sint (not 'seant' — esse is fully irregular in the present subjunctive).

questions.prompt: Give the 2nd person plural present passive subjunctive of amare.
questions.hint: Build the present active subjunctive base (amē-), then swap active endings for passive.
questions.explanation: amēminī — 2pl passive ending -minī is added to the present subjunctive stem amē-.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person singular present passive subjunctive of ducere.
questions.hint: 3rd conj. present subjunctive stem is dūcā-. 3sg passive = -tur.
questions.explanation: dūcātur. 3sg passive ending -tur applied to dūcā- stem.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person singular imperfect active subjunctive of amare.
questions.hint: Imperfect active subjunctive = present active infinitive + personal endings. 1sg = -m.
questions.explanation: Rule: take the present active infinitive (amāre) and add -m, -s, -t, -mus, -tis, -nt. → amārem.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person plural imperfect active subjunctive of monere.
questions.hint: Infinitive = monēre. Add -nt for 3pl.
questions.explanation: monēre + nt → monērent.

questions.prompt: Give the 2nd person singular imperfect active subjunctive of ducere.
questions.hint: Infinitive of dūcō is dūcere. 2sg = -s.
questions.explanation: dūcere + s → dūcerēs.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person plural imperfect active subjunctive of esse.
questions.hint: Infinitive of esse = esse. 1pl = -mus.
questions.explanation: esse + mus → essēmus.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person singular imperfect passive subjunctive of amare.
questions.hint: Imperfect passive subjunctive: use the infinitive stem + passive ending. 3sg passive = -tur.
questions.explanation: amāre- + tur = amārētur. Imperfect passive: infinitive + passive personal endings.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person plural imperfect passive subjunctive of monere.
questions.hint: monēre + passive 3pl ending -ntur.
questions.explanation: monēre + ntur → monērentur.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person singular perfect active subjunctive of amare. (Perf. stem: amāv-)
questions.hint: Perfect active subjunctive: perfect stem + -erim, -eris, -erit...
questions.explanation: Perfect active subjunctive = perfect stem + -erim/-erīs/-erit/-erīmus/-erītis/-erint. amāv + erim = amāverim.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person plural perfect active subjunctive of amare. (Perf. stem: amāv-)
questions.hint: Perfect active subjunctive 3pl ending = -erint.
questions.explanation: amāv + erint = amāverint.

questions.prompt: Give the 2nd person singular perfect active subjunctive of ducere. (Perf. stem: dūx-)
questions.hint: Perfect active subjunctive 2sg = -eris.
questions.explanation: dūx + eris = dūxeris.

questions.prompt: The perfect passive subjunctive is formed with the perfect passive participle + what?
questions.hint: Think: which subjunctive form of esse do you combine it with?
questions.explanation: Perfect passive subjunctive = PPP + present subjunctive of esse (sim/sīs/sit...). E.g., amātus sim = 'I may have been loved.'

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person singular perfect passive subjunctive of amare. (PPP: amātus)
questions.hint: PPP (singular, agrees with subject) + 3sg present subjunctive of esse.
questions.explanation: amātus sit (masc. sg.) — PPP + sit. Gender of PPP must agree with subject in actual use.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person singular pluperfect active subjunctive of amare. (Perf. stem: amāv-)
questions.hint: Pluperfect active subjunctive: perfect stem + -issem, -issēs, -isset...
questions.explanation: Pluperfect active subjunctive = perfect stem + -issem/-issēs/-isset/-issēmus/-issētis/-issent. amāv + issem = amāvissem.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person plural pluperfect active subjunctive of ducere. (Perf. stem: dūx-)
questions.hint: Pluperfect active subjunctive 3pl = -issent.
questions.explanation: dūx + issent = dūxissent.

questions.prompt: Give the 2nd person singular pluperfect active subjunctive of monere. (Perf. stem: monu-)
questions.hint: Pluperfect active subjunctive 2sg = -issēs.
questions.explanation: monu + issēs = monuissēs.

questions.prompt: The pluperfect passive subjunctive is formed with the perfect passive participle + what?
questions.hint: Same logic as perfect passive subjunctive, but use which tense of esse?
questions.explanation: Pluperfect passive subjunctive = PPP + imperfect subjunctive of esse (essem/essēs/esset...). E.g., amātus essem = 'I had been loved (subj.)'

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person singular pluperfect passive subjunctive of amare. (PPP: amātus)
questions.hint: PPP + 3sg imperfect subjunctive of esse.
questions.explanation: amātus esset — PPP + esset.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person plural pluperfect active subjunctive of audire. (Perf. stem: audīv-)
questions.hint: Pluperfect active subjunctive 1pl = -issēmus.
questions.explanation: audīv + issēmus = audīvissēmus.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense and mood of: amāret
questions.hint: Look at the ending and the infinitive stem pattern.
questions.explanation: amāret = infinitive amāre + t (3sg). This is imperfect active subjunctive. Compare indicative amābat — the -ba- infix is the giveaway for indicative.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense and mood of: dūxerint
questions.hint: The -eri- infix is characteristic of one subjunctive tense.
questions.explanation: dūx (perfect stem) + erint = perfect active subjunctive 3pl. Future perfect would be dūxerint too — in practice, context decides. On a form-ID question, 'perfect active subjunctive' is the expected answer.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense and mood of: monuissētis
questions.hint: -issē- is the tell-tale infix for one tense.
questions.explanation: monu (perf. stem) + issētis = pluperfect active subjunctive 2pl.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense and mood of: amēmus
questions.hint: The vowel change from -ā- in the stem is the hint.
questions.explanation: amēmus: the characteristic vowel -ā- of 1st conj. shifts to -ē- in the present subjunctive. 1pl = -mus.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense and mood of: amātus esset
questions.hint: This is a two-word periphrastic form.
questions.explanation: amātus (PPP) + esset (imperfect subjunctive of esse) = pluperfect passive subjunctive. If it were esset → pluperfect; if sit → perfect passive subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Identify the tense and mood of: amātus sit
questions.hint: PPP + which form of esse?
questions.explanation: amātus (PPP) + sit (3sg present subjunctive of esse) = perfect passive subjunctive.

questions.prompt:
Which form is indicative, not subjunctive?

amāret / amābat / amāret / amāverit
questions.hint: The indicative imperfect has a distinctive infix.
questions.explanation: amābat = imperfect INDICATIVE (3sg). The -bā- infix always signals indicative imperfect. amāret is subjunctive, amāverit/amāverim are perfect subjunctive.

questions.prompt:
Which form is subjunctive?

dūcit / dūcat / dūcēbat / dūxerat
questions.hint: Look for the -ā- vowel inserted into the 3rd conjugation stem.
questions.explanation: dūcat = present active subjunctive (3rd conj. takes -ā- in present subjunctive). dūcit = indicative pres., dūcēbat = indicative imperf., dūxerat = indicative pluperf.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct imperfect active subjunctive of esse?
questions.hint: Imperfect subjunctive = present infinitive + endings. What is esse's infinitive?
questions.explanation: esse + t = esset. erat = indicative imperfect (3sg). fuerit = perfect subjunctive. sit = present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Complete the paradigm: The four principal parts of amare are: amō, amāre, amāvī, _____
questions.hint: The 4th principal part is the perfect passive participle (PPP).
questions.explanation: amātum (supine/4PP) or amātus (PPP, masc. nom. sg.). The PPP amātus/a/um is built on this stem and is required to form passive perfect and pluperfect subjunctives.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person singular present active subjunctive of capere (3rd -io conj., perf. cēpī).
questions.hint: 3rd -iō verbs follow the 4th conjugation pattern in the present subjunctive.
questions.explanation: cap- + iā + t = capiat. 3rd -iō verbs (like 4th) insert -iā- in the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person singular imperfect active subjunctive of capere.
questions.hint: Imperfect subjunctive = present active infinitive + endings. What is capere's infinitive?
questions.explanation: capere + m = caperem. Note: the infinitive is capere, NOT *capire.

questions.prompt: Give the 3rd person plural present active subjunctive of posse (to be able).
questions.hint: posse is irregular. Its present subjunctive is: possim, possis, possit, possimus, possitis, _____
questions.explanation: possint — 3pl present subjunctive of posse. Note the double -s- (pos + sim paradigm).

questions.prompt: Give the 1st person singular imperfect active subjunctive of posse.
questions.hint: Infinitive of posse = posse. Apply the normal imperfect subjunctive rule.
questions.explanation: posse + m = possem. Imperfect subjunctive of posse: possem, possēs, posset, possēmus, possētis, possent.

questions.prompt: What tense and mood is portārentur?
questions.hint: The -re- + passive ending pattern signals which tense?
questions.explanation: portāre (infinitive) + ntur = portārentur. Imperfect passive subjunctive. The passive imperfect indicative would be portābantur.

questions.prompt: What tense and mood is ducāmur?
questions.hint: The -ā- infix in a 3rd conjugation verb is telling.
questions.explanation: dūcā + mur = present passive subjunctive 1pl. In 3rd conjugation, -ā- signals present subjunctive (compare future indicative dūcēmur with -ē-).
